release_notes:
Fix a latent layout-corruption bug that's been present since the leading-tab line format was introduced in 1.0.65 -- newly visible after 1.0.70's border refinements drew the eye to the inside of the log. Symptom: sending a Ready made the previously-newest incoming line lose its leading tab (body slid all the way to the left edge instead of aligning at the indent) AND made the new outgoing line render with the body kicked out to the timestamp column. Each send compounded the damage on the next line down.

Root cause: _append_ready_log used `recent2_start` (and `recent1_start`) as the insert position. Those marks point at the *body* start -- the char right after the leading '\t' -- because the emphasis font tags apply only to the body (so the timestamp stays at the log's default 10pt). Inserting text at that mark lands BETWEEN the existing line's leading tab and its body, splitting it into two malformed lines: the new outgoing entry ends up with two leading tabs (its own + the inherited one), which routes through the right-aligned tab2 stop instead of the left-aligned tab1; the displaced recent2 line loses its leading tab entirely. Both symptoms match the field report precisely.

Fix: insert at `recent2_start linestart` (and `recent1_start linestart`) so the new line lands at column 0 -- before the existing recent2 line's leading tab -- and the inserted trailing newline splits cleanly into a fresh whole line for the outgoing entry, with the original recent2 line shifting down with its leading tab intact. One-line change in chairside_ready_alert.py:_append_ready_log.

Persistence was not affected: _persist_ready_log_line writes the original well-formatted text the function was called with, not the corrupted in-widget result. ready_log.txt remained canonical throughout; restarting the app reloaded a clean layout. The corruption was purely a live-render artifact that this fix eliminates going forward.
